title: add-profiling-baselines-and-representative-workload-runners-reporting-pipeline
author: Maya Thompson
description: Add profiling baselines, representative workload runners, and a reporting pipeline for the benchmark lab. Motivation: provide a first-class baseline collection that can be scheduled and compared across hardware generations and model variants; enable representative workload runners for latency/throughput profiling; and surface standardized reports to the benchmark dashboard. Changes include: new 'runners' package with modular workload definitions; profiling collectors that capture per-token latency distribution, KV cache hit/miss, memory usage and kernel timings; a data transformation DAG that normalizes runners output into the reporting table; and CI guardrails to detect flaky workload runs. Checklist: [x] runner scaffolding and example workloads; [x] profiling baseline collector and local aggregator; [x] reporting pipeline DAG and BigQuery-compatible transforms; [x] unit + integration tests for runner and collector; [x] instrumentation + metric namespaces documented; [x] add CI rate limit for nightly schedules. This PR is intended to be backwards-compatible with existing benchmark-lab fixtures and to be the basis for automated profiling baselines in nightly jobs.
commits: Initial runner scaffolding and interface definitions (runners/)
Add profiling baseline collectors and local aggregator (profiling/collector.py)
Add reporting pipeline DAG and transforms (reporting/dags/benchmark_report.py)
CI: add flaky-test detection and rerun step (ci/benchmark.yml)
Fix: metric namespaces and tag consistency per reviewer feedback
review_comments: Dana Kim: Please split the collector into sampling vs continuous modes; continuous runs can overwhelm the local aggregator.
Arjun Patel: The BigQuery schema needs a version field and clearer metric namespaces so downstream dashboards don't break.
Lina Rodriguez: Can the representative workloads include a short-conversation variant (seq len ~64) to capture low-latency tail behavior?
author_replies: Maya Thompson: Split collector into sampling/continuous modes and added rate limiter config (profiling/collector.py).
Maya Thompson: Added schema version field and updated transforms to emit namespace as 'benchmark_lab.v2' (reporting/transforms/normalize.py).
Maya Thompson: Added short-conversation example workload and test that targets seq len 64 (runners/examples/convai_short.py).
Maya Thompson: Re-ran flaky integration test with additional timeouts and guard; CI re-run passed.
release_notes: Adds profiling baseline collection and representative workload runners to benchmark-lab; introduces reporting DAG and BigQuery transforms for normalized baseline metrics; adds CI guardrails for nightly profiling runs; non-breaking API changes to runner interfaces; schema versioning for reporting outputs.
